title: Mara and the Postcard
premise: Juniper Underhill, a ghostwriter who has spent ten years anonymously answering letters addressed to a dead woman's post office box, discovers his new neighbor, Mara Voss, is the sender of every letter he ever answered. She came looking for the stranger who kept her alive through her sister's wrongful conviction and death; instead she finds a man who has been hiding inside other people's stories since his own testimony helped convict an innocent man. As Juniper ghosts the memoir of the prosecutor who ruined both their lives, Mara's bakery lease and his buried guilt collide, forcing him to choose between exposing the truth and protecting the career that keeps him invisible. He confesses his role in her sister's case, loses her, then testifies at the reopened hearing anyway, winning justice too late for her sister but not too late for them; the final chapter closes with the bakery lease renewed in both their names.
about_author: Marguerite Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing testimonies before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town where she volunteers with an innocence project, and this is her third novel.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Learns
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He finishes ghosting a celebrity memoir, reflecting on his creed that the heart is trainable and containable. A new lease on a cheap apartment above a failing bakery signals a fresh start. Emotional beat: controlled detachment masking old wounds.

chapters.title: Return to Sender
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She arrives in town with a shoebox of unanswered letters and takes over the bakery below Juniper's apartment, chasing the anonymous correspondent who wrote back to her for a decade. Emotional beat: stubborn hope disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Flour and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. First meeting: Mara mistakes him for a health inspector, then a drifter. He recognizes nothing yet, but her voice snags something familiar. Emotional beat: wary curiosity undercut by self-protective irony.

chapters.title: Letters to a Dead Address
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flashback chapter: her sister Ivy's conviction, prison years, and the postcard that started the correspondence. The letters were her lifeline; the writer never gave a name. Emotional beat: grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Question
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He finds one of his own old letters in Mara's bakery, left as decoration. Panic: she is the letter-writer, and she is hunting him. He decides to stay silent. Emotional beat: dread curdling into cowardice.

chapters.title: Sourdough Confessions
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Late-night baking sessions turn into friendship as Juniper helps fix her failing ovens and books. She almost tells him about the letters; he deflects. Emotional beat: intimacy growing on uneven ground.

chapters.title: A Commission in Gray
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A lucrative offer arrives: ghost the memoir of District Attorney Alden Crane, the prosecutor from Ivy Voss's trial. Taking it means facing the case he buried. He accepts, telling himself it's just money. Emotional beat: rationalized self-betrayal.

chapters.title: What Ivy Knew
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She begins reviewing her sister's trial records for an innocence-project volunteer, discovering inconsistencies Crane suppressed. Her grief sharpens into purpose. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Truths, One Kitchen
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Working from Mara's bakery by day on Crane's memoir, he reads the trial transcript and realizes his own decade-old statement was twisted into false corroboration. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a drowned thing.

chapters.title: The Man in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A sleepless night; he drafts a confession letter to Mara a dozen times and burns each one. His creed about the containable heart collapses. Emotional beat: the first honest reckoning with himself.

chapters.title: Crane's Version
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She interviews Crane publicly at a book event, probing his account of the Voss case. He is charming, rehearsed, and lies fluently. She leaves certain now that he hid evidence. Emotional beat: cold clarity beneath civility.

chapters.title: Lease Terms
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The bakery's landlord gives Mara sixty days. Juniper quietly considers buying the building to save her, another act done in disguise rather than truth. Emotional beat: love expressed as concealment.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A near-kiss interrupted when she finds Crane's draft manuscript pages in Juniper's bag. Suspicion blooms: why is he writing the prosecutor's book? Emotional beat: warmth cracking into doubt.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Mara confronts him; cornered, he admits he answered her letters for ten years but still hides his role in the trial. Joy and betrayal arrive in the same hour. Emotional beat: euphoria poisoned by omission.

chapters.title: Half a Truth
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She learns from the innocence file that a witness statement matching Juniper's phrasing helped convict Ivy. She connects it to him and walks out without a word. Emotional beat: devastation colder than anger.

chapters.title: Crane's Leverage
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Crane, sensing Juniper's wavering, threatens to expose his falsified statement and destroy what's left of his career if the memoir turns disloyal. Emotional beat: trapped between two ruinous loyalties.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ivy's case is reopened on fresh evidence. Juniper must decide whether to testify. Mara, in the gallery, doesn't know if he'll come. Emotional beat: suspended breath, the arc's highest tension.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the stand, he recants his coerced statement, names Crane's suppression, and forfeits his anonymity and career in one breath. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into release.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Ivy is posthumously exonerated; Crane is referred for prosecution. Mara watches Juniper leave the courthouse alone, unsure whether justice can be shared. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Empty Ovens
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Days of silence. He writes Mara one true letter, unsigned, and slides it under her door, then packs to leave town. Emotional beat: humility without expectation.

chapters.title: The Last Postcard
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She reads the letter through the night, recognizing the handwriting she has loved for a decade. At dawn she finds him loading his car and answers ten years of letters with one sentence: stay. Emotional beat: forgiveness chosen, not owed.

chapters.title: Both Names on the Lease
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Spring: the bakery reopens with a new sign bearing two names, Juniper's memoir under his own name on the bestseller list, and a framed postcard by the register. Emotional beat: belonging earned, survival paid for, hearts uncontained at last.
